headline: Stott's bases-loaded double in the 10th beats Braves
recap: The Phillies needed extra innings to beat the Braves on the road. Atlanta had erased a 4-2 deficit with two runs in the bottom of the eighth off Jeff Hoffman and Gregory Soto to tie it at 4-4. In the 10th, pinch-runner Johan Rojas and Bryce Harper pulled off a double steal before Bryson Stott's two-out, bases-loaded double off A.J. Minter scored them both for a 6-4 lead. Ozzie Albies' sacrifice fly brought Atlanta's automatic runner home in the bottom half, but Matt Strahm retired Austin Riley to close it out, 6-5.

Aaron Nola started for the Phillies and allowed two runs on six hits over six innings, striking out eight without a walk. Braves starter Bryce Elder lasted only 3.2 innings, walking five and giving up two home runs.

Nick Castellanos accounted for three of the Phillies' six runs, homering in the second and again in the fourth to finish 2 for 5 with three RBIs. Craig Kimbrel worked a scoreless ninth for the win, and Strahm picked up the save.
